Funding Opportunity Purpose

The purpose of this Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) is to conduct secondary data analyses using existing data collected from humans participating in vision-related clinical trials, epidemiologic, and other clinical research studies or represented in clinical and health care database resources (e.g., electronic health records). This NOFO may be used to develop new statistical methodologies or test hypotheses using existing data, but this NOFO must not be used to support the collection of new data. This NOFO encourages applications from institutions/organizations that propose to conduct vision-related secondary analyses of data collected from humans.  Applications may be related to, but must be distinct from, the specific aims of the original data collection.

Applicants should consider the relevance of their proposed analyses to NEI programs and priorities as described in the NEI Strategic Plan: Vision for the Future.

Objectives and Scope

A typical project supported under this NOFO is expected to make substantial progress towards having at least one vision-related manuscript submitted to a peer-reviewed journal within the first year.

Research Strategy:

Please clearly address the following:

  1. Explain how the proposed secondary analyses provide important insight into vision health problems.
  2. Provide details of the existing data (data sets or databases) and describe how these data will be utilized to address the project's specific aims and NEI’s mission. Explain how the data are of sufficient quality to address the specific aims of the study and currently exist in analyzable format (i.e., structured and reasonably cleaned). Include plans to control or account for potential biases and deficiencies in data (e.g., missing, inconsistent or implausible data; misclassification and information bias; selection bias; potential confounding).
  3. As applicable, demonstrate how the proposed new methodologies may improve future analyses of vision-related research data and provide evidence that the new approaches are needed.
  4. Describe specific milestones and timelines for data analysis, manuscript(s) preparation and submission to peer-reviewed journals. These milestones must include at least two manuscript submissions: one submitted for peer review prior to submission of the Research Performance Progress Report (RPPR) and one manuscript submitted prior to the submission of the Final Progress Report.

1. Criteria

Only the review criteria described below will be considered in the review process. Applications submitted to the NIH in support of the NIH mission are evaluated for scientific and technical merit through the NIH peer review system.
